metadata.title: Game State Management and Game Loop

story.iWant: I want the game to run a continuous game loop that updates game state
story.soThat: so that the evening timer counts down and game mechanics function properly

tasks.task: Create useGameLoop hook - Create `src/hooks/useGameLoop.ts` file - Implement hook that wraps `requestAnimationFrame` - Calculate delta time for frame-independent updates - Handle cleanup (cancel animation frame) in useEffect cleanup - Follow architecture patterns [Source: docs/architecture.md#Game-Loop-Lifecycle]

Implement Page Visibility API pause/resume - Listen for document visibility changes - Pause game loop when tab becomes inactive (`document.hidden === true`) - Resume game loop when tab becomes active - Update `isPaused` state in GameContext - Prevent timer updates while paused

Implement game state updates in game loop - Update evening timer (decrease by delta time, use EVENING_DURATION constant) [Source: docs/sprint-artifacts/1-5-game-constants-and-configuration.md] - Update «Затишок» meter (decrease by COZINESS_DECAY_RATE * delta time) [Source: docs/sprint-artifacts/1-5-game-constants-and-configuration.md] - Update active event timers (count down by delta time, Story 2.5 will handle this fully) - Clamp values to valid ranges (coziness: 0-100, timeRemaining: >= 0) - Update GameContext state via context update functions

Integrate game loop with GameContext - Use GameContext from `src/contexts/GameContext.tsx` (created in Story 1.3) - Update game state using context update functions (not direct state mutation) - Ensure React re-renders when state changes - Read initial game state from context - Read player level from ProgressionContext (for level-based bonuses)

Initialize game state when evening starts - Create function to initialize/reset game state - Set initial coziness (60 or based on level bonuses from Story 3.3) - Set initial timeRemaining from EVENING_DURATION constant [Source: docs/sprint-artifacts/1-5-game-constants-and-configuration.md] - Reset score to 0 - Reset activeEvents to empty array - Set isPlaying: true, isPaused: false, gameOver: false - Ensure GameState matches type definition from `src/types/game.ts`

Performance optimization and testing - Verify 60 FPS performance (no frame drops during gameplay) - Ensure delta time calculation is accurate (handle frame rate variations) - Test pause/resume functionality (tab visibility changes) - Test cleanup on component unmount (no memory leaks) - Verify game loop stops when gameOver is true

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given the game is initialized, When I start an evening, Then the game loop starts using `requestAnimationFrame`, And the game loop updates every frame (~60 FPS): Evening timer decreases by delta time, «Затишок» meter decreases by decay rate (if no events affecting it), Active event timers count down, Game state is updated in GameContext

Given the game loop is running, When the browser tab becomes inactive, Then the game loop pauses (using Page Visibility API), And when the tab becomes active again, the game loop resumes, And timers do not count down while paused
Given the game component unmounts, When the component is removed from the DOM, Then the animation frame is cancelled, And no memory leaks occur (cleanup in useEffect)

Given the game loop is running, When the game loop integrates with React, Then it uses `useGameLoop` hook that wraps requestAnimationFrame, And it updates GameContext state via context update functions, And it triggers React re-renders when state changes, And it maintains 60 FPS performance (no frame drops)

Given an evening starts, When initial game state is set, Then game state structure matches GameState interface from types [Source: docs/architecture.md#Data-Architecture], And initial values are: coziness: 60 (or based on level bonuses from ProgressionContext), timeRemaining: 60-90 seconds (from EVENING_DURATION constant), score: 0, activeEvents: [], isPlaying: true, isPaused: false, gameOver: false

doc.title: Story 2.1: Game State Management and Game Loop

docs.doc: Story specification with acceptance criteria, tasks, and dev notes. Includes detailed implementation guidance for creating game loop hook, Page Visibility API integration, and React Context integration.

Architecture patterns for game loop lifecycle: Start with requestAnimationFrame in useEffect, Update game state to trigger re-renders, Cleanup by canceling animation frame in useEffect cleanup. Use Page Visibility API to pause when tab inactive.
Architecture decision to use requestAnimationFrame for 60 FPS (not setInterval). Standard for browser games, provides smooth frame rate, integrates with browser rendering cycle.

Architecture decision record explaining rationale for React Context over Redux. Simple state management needs, no extra dependencies, sufficient for hackathon scope. Context updates trigger React re-renders automatically.
GameState interface structure definition. Includes coziness, timeRemaining, score, activeEvents, isPlaying, isPaused, gameOver properties. Initial state values specified.

Game loop optimization: Use requestAnimationFrame for smooth 60 FPS, batch state updates to minimize re-renders, use React.memo for expensive components. Memory management: clean up event listeners on unmount, cancel animation frames on cleanup.
Project structure showing hooks directory location: `src/hooks/useGameLoop.ts`. File naming conventions: camelCase for hook files. Hook should follow React hook rules.

PRD specifications for game mechanics: Evening timer (60-90 seconds), «Затишок» meter (0-100, decreases over time), event timers, game loop requirements. Win/lose conditions based on timer and coziness.
Epic-level story definition with acceptance criteria and technical notes. Prerequisites: Story 1.3 (Game Context), Story 1.5 (Constants). Follow architecture document "Game Loop" section.

Previous story learnings: Constants file ready for use. EVENING_DURATION: 75 seconds, COZINESS_START: 60, COZINESS_DECAY_RATE: 0.5 per second. Helper functions available: `getMaxSimultaneousEvents(level)`, `getEventTimerDuration(level)`. Import pattern: Use named exports.

doc.title: Story 1.3: React Context Setup for Game State

docs.doc: Previous story learnings: GameContext available with GameState type and update functions. Use `useContext(GameContext)` to access state and update functions. State updates via context trigger React re-renders automatically. ProgressionContext available for level/XP data.

Previous story learnings: GameState type definition complete and ready. TypeScript strict mode enabled. Import pattern: Use `import type` for type-only imports. Types exported from `src/types/game.ts`.

artifact.reason: GameState interface defines the structure for game state. Includes coziness, timeRemaining, score, activeEvents, isPlaying, isPaused, gameOver properties. Required for game loop state updates.

GameContext provides game state and update functions. Hook must use context update functions (setCoziness, setTimeRemaining, setScore, setPlaying, setPaused, setGameOver, updateGameState) to modify state. Context triggers React re-renders when state changes.
GameStateContextValue interface defines context value structure. Includes gameState and all update functions. Hook should use these functions to update state, not direct mutations.
useGame hook provides access to GameContext. Hook must use this to access game state and update functions. Throws error if used outside GameProvider.
ProgressionContext provides player level for level-based bonuses. Hook should read player level to determine initial coziness and evening duration based on level bonuses (future Story 3.3).
EVENING_DURATION constant (75 seconds) used for initial timeRemaining. Import from constants file for initial game state setup.
COZINESS_START constant (60) used for initial coziness value. Import from constants file for initial game state setup.
COZINESS_DECAY_RATE constant (0.5 per second) used for coziness decay in game loop. Multiply by delta time for frame-independent updates.
Hooks directory location. Currently exists from Story 1.3 setup. Will contain useGameLoop.ts file.

constraints.constraint: Game Loop Pattern: Use `requestAnimationFrame` for 60 FPS (not setInterval) [Source: docs/architecture.md#Decision-Summary]. Calculate delta time for frame-independent updates (ensures consistent game speed regardless of frame rate). Use Page Visibility API to pause when tab inactive [Source: docs/architecture.md#Game-Loop-Lifecycle]. Cleanup animation frame in useEffect cleanup to prevent memory leaks [Source: docs/architecture.md#Game-Loop-Lifecycle].

State Management Pattern: Use React Context API for game state (GameContext created in Story 1.3) [Source: docs/architecture.md#ADR-002]. Update state via context update functions (not direct mutations). State changes trigger React re-renders automatically. Read initial state and level bonuses from contexts [Source: docs/architecture.md#Integration-Points].

Hook Pattern: Implement `useGameLoop` hook in `src/hooks/useGameLoop.ts` [Source: docs/architecture.md#Project-Structure]. Hook should accept dependencies (isPlaying, isPaused, gameOver). Hook should return nothing (side effects only) or return current frame info. Follow React hook rules (call at top level, include dependencies in useEffect).

Performance Considerations: Maintain 60 FPS (no frame drops). Use delta time for frame-independent updates (ensures game speed consistency). Minimize state updates (only update when values actually change). Avoid expensive calculations in game loop (pre-calculate or cache). Use GPU-accelerated CSS transforms for rendering (not handled here, but prepare for Story 2.3).

Initial State Values: coziness: 60 (or based on level bonuses from ProgressionContext), timeRemaining: 60-90 seconds (from EVENING_DURATION constant), score: 0, activeEvents: [], isPlaying: true, isPaused: false, gameOver: false. GameState structure must match GameState interface from `src/types/game.ts`.

Constants Usage: Import constants from `src/utils/constants.ts`: EVENING_DURATION, COZINESS_START, COZINESS_DECAY_RATE. Use helper functions for level-dependent lookups if needed. Follow export pattern from Story 1.5 (named exports).

Page Visibility API: Listen for `document.visibilitychange` event. Check `document.hidden` property to determine if tab is inactive. Pause game loop when `document.hidden === true`. Resume when `document.hidden === false`. Update `isPaused` state in GameContext. Prevent timer updates while paused.

Delta Time Calculation: Calculate delta time as difference between current frame time and previous frame time. Handle frame rate variations (some frames may take longer). Use delta time for all time-based updates (timer countdown, coziness decay). Ensure frame-independent game speed.
Value Clamping: Clamp coziness to valid range (0-100). Clamp timeRemaining to valid range (>= 0). Ensure values never go below minimum or above maximum. Use Math.max and Math.min for clamping.

TypeScript Strict Mode: TypeScript strict mode is enabled - all types must be properly defined. Use `import type` for type-only imports. No `any` types allowed. Hook must have proper return type (void or frame info type).

interface.name: GameState
interface.signature: interface GameState { coziness: number; timeRemaining: number; score: number; activeEvents: GameEvent[]; isPlaying: boolean; isPaused: boolean; gameOver: boolean; }

interface.name: GameStateContextValue
interface.signature: interface GameStateContextValue { gameState: GameState; setCoziness: (value: number) => void; setTimeRemaining: (value: number) => void; setScore: (value: number) => void; setPlaying: (playing: boolean) => void; setPaused: (paused: boolean) => void; setGameOver: (gameOver: boolean) => void; updateGameState: (updates: Partial<GameState>) => void; ... }

tests.standards: TypeScript compilation must succeed with no errors. Use `npm run build` or `npx tsc --noEmit` to verify. No TypeScript errors or warnings in hook file. Test game loop starts and stops correctly. Test pause/resume functionality with Page Visibility API. Test cleanup on component unmount (no memory leaks). Verify 60 FPS performance (no frame drops). Test delta time calculation accuracy. Test value clamping (coziness 0-100, timeRemaining >= 0). Consider using Vitest for unit tests (from architecture document), but manual testing is acceptable for this foundational story.
tests.locations: Test files should be co-located with source files: `src/hooks/useGameLoop.test.ts` (optional for this story). Manual testing via temporary test components is acceptable.
